newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ford targets the young and trendy with Ka.
newsitem.headline: Ford targets the young and trendy with Ka.

text.p: Ford on Monday presented its Ka model, a so-called minicar that will compete with vehicles like Renault's Twingo and Mercedes-Benz's new car, and said it was the first of a new line.
"Ka is Ford's first New Edge design production car," chairman and chief executive officer Alex Trotman said.

"New Edge is a Ford design style that features edge highlights where rounded sections meet. We think it will have the same impact on the next 10 years of automotive styling as our aerodynamic designs had on the last 10 years," he said.
Unveiling the car to around 500 journalists and industry analysts on the Champs Elysees a day before the opening of the Paris car show, Trotman said it had been developed in just over two years.
Ka means vitality in old Egyptian.
Using the musical slogan "We are young" in a movie clip with ballet dancers as well as live acrobatic acts, Ford is targeting the Ka at the young and trendy.

Initial reaction to the Ka, which was shown as a prototype at the Geneva car show in 1994, has been enough for Ford to try to boost production at its Valencia plant in Spain from initial volumes of 200,000 per year.

"The reaction to it (Ka) has been so strong that we think that 200,000 will not do it. There is a very urgent study under way right now with component, engines, transmission and assembly to see how high we can get it," Trotman said.
"I don't know whether we can get 240,000 or 250,000 in the first year but that would be the general magnitude, I suspect," he told Reuters.
Ford has also decided to build the Ka in Brazil but the exact location and production capacity has not yet been decided.
The Ka is 3.6 metres (11 ft 10 in) long and uses a 1.3 litre (0.2860 Imp gallons) Endura petrol injection engine. Ford has not yet disclosed its price.
Trotman said the small car market in Europe is expected to grow from 32 percent of the total market to 35 percent by the year 2000 -- or from 3.85 million cars to 4.5 million.

"I see the European market somewhere up there in the high 13 (million), 14 (million). It looks quite good to us. The industry is really doing quite well, with a little bouncing up and down in Britain and a little nervousness in France now that the (government) incentive programme is stopping," he said.
Monday was the last day to take advantage of state rebate offers for French buyers turning in old vehicles.
